chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) appointed Shurayh as judge, he stipulated with him that he should not execute the judgment until he presented it to him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What condition did Imam Ali impose on his judges regarding the execution of verdicts?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the early Islamic model of judicial oversight, where Imam Ali (peace be upon him) retained final authority by requiring Shurayh to present all verdicts for approval before execution. This condition underscores the Shia concept of the Imam’s comprehensive knowledge and his role as the ultimate arbiter in legal matters, ensuring that judicial decisions align with divine justice and prophetic tradition.
